sn47.51-62:1.1: “Bhikkhus, just as the river Ganges slants, slopes, and inclines towards the east,
sn47.51-62:1.2: so too a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the four establishments of mindfulness slants, slopes, and inclines towards Nibbāna.
sn47.51-62:2.1: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu develop and cultivate the four establishments of mindfulness so that he slants, slopes, and inclines towards Nibbāna?
sn47.51-62:2.2: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body …
sn47.51-62:2.5: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.51-62:2.6: It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu develops and cultivates the four establishments of mindfulness so that he slants, slopes, and inclines towards Nibbāna.”
sn47.51-62:2.7: (The remaining suttas of this vagga are to be similarly elaborated parallel to 45:92-102.)
sn47.51-62:3.1: Six about slanting to the east
sn47.51-62:3.2: And six about slanting to the ocean.
sn47.51-62:3.3: These two sixes make up twelve:
